one_month_reasoning: The window runs to the last close before 2026-11-01 (Fri 2026-10-30). Lattice's Q3 2026 report is expected around 2026-11-03 per earnings calendars, so most likely just outside the window. Lattice has reported Q3 in late October before, though, so there is some chance it lands inside. Other scheduled drivers are macro and sector events: peer semiconductor earnings in late October (TXN, NXPI, MCHP, ON, AMD) and possible news on Section 232 Phase-2 chip tariffs, which Commerce flagged on 2026-09-02. Momentum is mixed. The stock bounced +16% from its September low to $134 and rose 4% on the last day, but it is still 15% below its June high. I have no directional edge, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal centered at $134.5 with sigma 0.17 (61% annual vol / 3.5). That is a touch above the usual monthly width to allow for a possible early earnings date and tariff headlines.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (2028E EPS $3.30 x 40x = $132, discounted lightly) and a FCF-yield cross-check (NTM-at-horizon FCF/share ~$3.6 at a 2.6% yield = $138). Weights are 60/40, giving ~$136 for the 12-month fair value.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Forward EPS seen at Oct-2027 (CY2028E) $3.30 x 40x = $132. Cross-check: CY2027E EPS $2.75 x 49x historical mean = $135. Average ~$134.

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue ~$1.28B (FPGA ~$1.03B: the ~$0.94B Q4-26 run rate +10%; AMI ~$0.25B). Non-GAAP op margin ~40%, below Q2's ~38% op/43% EBITDA plus software mix, gives ~$510M. Interest ~$45M on a ~$950M term loan being paid down. Tax ~13%. Shares ~143M (~137M pre-deal + 5.2-6.1M issued to AMI).
~20% EPS growth, between consensus 27% revenue CAGR (TIKR) and a slowdown as the AI data-center build matures. Mgmt targets $3B revenue by 2030.

LSCC's historical mean P/E is ~49x (TIKR), currently ~62x NTM. I apply a ~20% discount for added leverage, the lower-multiple software mix from AMI, and base rates. In the 2023-24 FPGA down-cycle the stock fell from ~$97 to ~$45 and the multiple compressed hard (Twelve Data price history).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FCF/share ~$3.6 (NTM at horizon: ~$1.45B revenue x ~35% FCF margin / 143M shares) at a 2.6% FCF yield = ~$138

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2's 40% margin, less cash interest on acquisition debt and integration costs.
The CY2027E $1.28B grown at ~20% for the next four quarters.
MarketBeat's $18.36B market cap at $134 implies ~137M, plus 5.2-6.1M AMI consideration shares if they are not already included.
The ~49x mean P/E history implies a ~2-2.5% earnings/FCF yield for LSCC in non-bust years. I add a bit for leverage, which gives 2.6%.

bear.story: The FPGA cycle rolls over as AI-server and industrial inventory digests, the AMI integration disappoints, and leverage plus a 2027 recession (Kalshi ~41%) compress the multiple to ~30x on ~$2.4 EPS. This repeats the 2023-24 pattern, when LSCC fell ~55% peak to trough.

base.story: Revenue reaches ~$1.3B in 2027 with FPGA growing modestly and AMI +25%. EPS ~$2.75 and the multiple de-rates to ~40x forward on 2028 EPS. The stock ends roughly flat to slightly up.

bull.story: AI data-center attach (board management, security FPGAs plus AMI firmware) keeps compounding toward the $3B 2030 target. 2028 EPS reaches ~$4 and the stock holds a ~55x premium multiple. That continues the 2019-21 style re-rating, when 12-month gains above 80% were often followed by further 30-100%.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$88 the market would be valuing LSCC at ~32x a $2.75 2027 EPS, near the bottom of its post-2020 range. That level held only in the 2023-24 inventory bust. It would most likely mean FPGA revenue is shrinking again or the AMI deal and its ~$950M debt are going wrong, not ordinary volatility. It is also below the August-September 2026 lows (~$104-112) by a wide margin.

reasoning: Base rates first. Across 88 rolling 12-month windows of LSCC's own monthly history (2016-2026, Twelve Data), the median return is +49% with a 10th-90th percentile range of -24% to +150%. That is inflated by the 2019-21 re-rating from $6 to $77. Of 24 windows that followed a >80% one-year gain, 14 kept rising (mostly 2020-21), but the most recent episodes (2022-23 after the 2021 run) gave -2% to -51%. Long-run vol is ~49% annualized and the recent realized figure is 61%. On fundamentals, Q2 2026 revenue was $201M (+62%) with non-GAAP EPS $0.53, and Q3 guides $255M including AMI with EPS $0.56. Management targets a $1.2B exit run rate and $3B revenue by 2030. My CY2027 EPS estimate is ~$2.75, so at $134 the stock trades at ~49x, right on its historical mean P/E (TIKR). Sell-side mean target is ~$147 (MarketBeat, range $80-180). The stock already showed it can drop ~30% in two months on leverage worries (June $157 to Aug ~$112) despite beats. Fair value is ~$136, near the current price, so I center the distribution with a median ~$131-134 and a mean ~$140 (scenarios: 25% bear $78 / 50% base $140 / 25% bull $215). I model it as an 85/15 mixture: a lognormal with median $142 and sigma 0.50, plus a 15% 'bust' component with median $85, to fatten the left tail for an FPGA down-cycle, tariffs and the Kalshi 2027 recession odds. Research limits: the Business Wire release and some aggregator pages were blocked (403/503). I could not read Kalshi market volumes directly, so the 41% figure comes from a secondary aggregator snippet, and Twelve Data estimates were paywalled.
